locations.help: Select one or more locations to analyse. Each location represents a specific geographic point with extracted climate data.

scenarios.general_help: Climate scenarios represent different possible futures based on socioeconomic pathways and greenhouse gas emissions.
scenarios.agcd: AGCD (Australian Gridded Climate Data): Observational data from Bureau of Meteorology weather stations. This is real historical climate data, not model output.
scenarios.historical: Historical: CMIP6 climate model simulation of past climate (typically 1850-2014). Used to validate model performance against observations.
scenarios.ssp1-26: SSP1-26 (Sustainability - Taking the Green Road): Low challenges to mitigation and adaptation. The world shifts gradually toward a more sustainable path, emphasising inclusive development. CO₂ emissions decline to net zero around 2075. Global warming likely limited to 1.8°C by 2100.
scenarios.ssp2-45: SSP2-45 (Middle of the Road): Medium challenges to mitigation and adaptation. Social, economic and technological trends do not shift markedly from historical patterns. CO₂ emissions remain around current levels before declining mid-century. Global warming likely around 2.7°C by 2100.
scenarios.ssp3-70: SSP3-70 (Regional Rivalry - A Rocky Road): High challenges to mitigation and adaptation. Resurgent nationalism, concerns about competitiveness and security lead to regional blocs. CO₂ emissions double by 2100. Global warming likely around 3.6°C by 2100.
scenarios.ssp5-85: SSP5-85 (Fossil-fuelled Development - Taking the Highway): High challenges for mitigation, low challenges for adaptation. Rapid technological progress and development of human capital with economy and lifestyles based on abundant fossil fuel use. CO₂ emissions triple by 2075. Global warming likely around 4.4°C by 2100.

display_mode.help: Choose how to display the data values.
display_mode.values: Absolute Values: Show actual measured or modelled values (e.g. temperature in °C, rainfall in mm).
display_mode.baseline: Baseline (start year): Show change relative to the first year in the selected range. Useful for seeing trends over time.
display_mode.deltas: Deltas vs baseline: Show difference between each scenario and the baseline scenario. Useful for comparing how scenarios diverge.

display_options.smooth_values: Apply rolling average smoothing to reduce year-to-year variability and reveal long-term trends more clearly. Useful for noisy metrics like rainfall.
display_options.smoothing_window: Number of years to include in the rolling average. Larger windows create smoother curves but may hide short-term variations. Odd numbers (e.g. 9) keep the smoothed value centred on the middle year.
display_options.table_interval: Control how many years to show in the data table. Larger intervals reduce table size for long time periods.
display_options.15c_shading: Display a reference line showing when regional temperature reaches the level corresponding to 1.5°C global warming above pre-industrial. Regional warming is amplified (~1.15× global warming for this location).
display_options.horizon_shading: Shade the chart background to show three future time horizons: Short-term (2021-2040), Mid-term (2041-2060), and Long-term (2061-2080). Helps visualise when changes are expected to occur.

year_range.help: Select the time period to analyse. Historical data typically covers 1850-2014, while future scenarios extend to 2100.
year_range.start_year: First year to include in analysis.
year_range.end_year: Last year to include in analysis.

time_horizons.help: Define custom time periods for analysis. These horizons appear in the Dashboard and can be highlighted on charts.
time_horizons.planning_horizon: Final year for long-term planning or infrastructure design (e.g. 2100).

metric_type.help: Select the climate variable category to analyse.
metric_type.temp: Temperature: Daily average (tas), maximum (tasmax), heat thresholds, and extreme temperature metrics.
metric_type.rain: Rainfall/Precipitation: Daily totals, seasonal accumulations, wet day frequencies, dry spells, and extreme rainfall events.
metric_type.wind: Wind Speed: Daily average wind speed, extreme wind events, and wind percentiles.
metric_type.humidity: Humidity: Relative humidity (RH) and vapour pressure deficit (VPD). Important for heat stress, fire danger, and plant water stress.

metric_names.help: Select specific metrics within the chosen variable type. Multiple metrics can be compared simultaneously.

temp.average: Average: Mean daily temperature (tas). Key indicator of overall warming trend.
temp.max_day: Max Day: Highest daily maximum temperature (tasmax) in the period. Indicates extreme heat events.
temp.avg_max: Avg Max: Average of daily maximum temperatures. Important for daytime heat exposure.
temp.5day_avg_max: 5-Day Avg Max: Highest 5-day average of maximum temperatures. Indicates sustained heatwave conditions.
temp.days_37c: Days ≥37°C ≥3h est: Estimated number of days where temperature exceeds 37°C for at least 3 hours. Heat stress threshold for humans and agriculture.
temp.days_40c: Days ≥40°C ≥3h est: Estimated number of days where temperature exceeds 40°C for at least 3 hours. Extreme heat threshold with significant health and infrastructure impacts.

rain.total: Total: Sum of daily precipitation (raw model output). Annual totals show overall water availability; seasonal totals show monsoon/dry season patterns. For SSP scenarios, also see 'Total (BC)' for bias-corrected values.
rain.total_bc: Total (BC): Bias-corrected precipitation. Correction factors calculated from AGCD vs Historical comparison (1990-2014). Accounts for systematic model underestimation during wet seasons (+44% DJF) and overestimation during dry seasons (-13% JJA/MAM). Only available for SSP scenarios. BC = Bias Corrected.
rain.max_day: Max Day: Highest daily rainfall in the period. Indicates extreme rainfall/flood potential. For SSP scenarios, 'Max Day (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.min_day: Min Day: Lowest daily rainfall (typically 0 mm). For SSP scenarios, 'Min Day (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.max_5day: Max 5-Day: Highest 5-day cumulative rainfall. Important for flood risk and soil saturation. For SSP scenarios, 'Max 5-Day (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.min_5day: Min 5-Day: Lowest 5-day cumulative rainfall. Indicates dry spell intensity. For SSP scenarios, 'Min 5-Day (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.r10mm: R10mm: Number of days with rainfall ≥10 mm. Moderate rainfall days. For SSP scenarios, 'R10mm (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.r20mm: R20mm: Number of days with rainfall ≥20 mm. Heavy rainfall days. For SSP scenarios, 'R20mm (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.
rain.cdd: CDD: Consecutive Dry Days - longest sequence of days with rainfall <1 mm. Key drought indicator. For SSP scenarios, 'CDD (BC)' shows bias-corrected values.

wind.average: Average: Mean daily wind speed. Baseline wind climate.
wind.max_day: Max Day: Highest daily wind speed. Indicates extreme wind events.
wind.95th_percentile: 95th Percentile: Wind speed exceeded on only 5% of days. Useful for structural design and wind energy assessment.

humidity.average_rh: Average RH: Mean relative humidity (%). High RH increases heat stress and reduces evaporative cooling.
humidity.average_vpd: Average VPD: Mean vapour pressure deficit (kPa). High VPD indicates dry air and increased plant water stress. Critical for agriculture and fire danger.

seasons.help: Select seasons to analyse. Southern Hemisphere seasons are defined astronomically.
seasons.annual: Annual: Full calendar year (Jan-Dec). Shows overall trends without seasonal breakdown.
seasons.djf: DJF: Summer (December, January, February). Wet season for northern Australia; typically warmest period.
seasons.mam: MAM: Autumn (March, April, May). Transition to dry season; moderate temperatures.
seasons.jja: JJA: Winter (June, July, August). Dry season for northern Australia; typically coolest period.
seasons.son: SON: Spring (September, October, November). Transition to wet season; temperatures rising.

dashboard.help: Summary view comparing selected scenarios across multiple metrics and time horizons. Useful for identifying which scenarios show greatest changes and when those changes occur.
dashboard.metric_type_selector: Choose which climate variable to display in the heatmap matrix.
dashboard.horizon_columns: Each column represents a different time period. Colours show the magnitude of change relative to the baseline period.

global_tab.help: Analyse the timing and impacts of reaching 1.5°C global warming above pre-industrial levels. This threshold is a key target in the Paris Agreement. Regional warming is typically amplified relative to global mean warming.
global_tab.warming_year: Shows when each scenario is projected to cross the 1.5°C global warming threshold.
global_tab.regional_impact: Shows the regional temperature at the time of reaching 1.5°C global warming. Regional warming is amplified by a factor of ~1.15 for this location.
global_tab.exceedance_years: Number of years where global temperature exceeds 1.5°C above pre-industrial. Higher emissions scenarios exceed the threshold earlier and for longer.

user_guide.help: Comprehensive scientific documentation covering: data sources, climate scenarios, metrics definitions, uncertainty quantification, bias correction methodology, and interpretation guidance.

scenario_naming.ssp: SSP: Shared Socioeconomic Pathway - describes different socioeconomic development trends.
scenario_naming.numbers: First number (1-5): Socioeconomic pathway. Second number (26-85): Approximate radiative forcing in 2100 (W/m²), which relates to warming level.

general.bias_correction_note: Bias correction is applied during metrics generation. For SSP scenarios, both raw and bias-corrected versions of all rain metrics are available. Look for metrics with '(BC)' suffix (e.g. 'Total (BC)', 'Max Day (BC)') to view bias-corrected data. Correction factors are calculated from AGCD (observations) vs Historical (model) comparison during 1990-2014.
general.data_quality: All data has been quality-controlled and validated. Missing values are not permitted. Climate model data is from CMIP6 (Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6).
general.citation: Data: CMIP6 ACCESS-CM2 (CSIRO/BoM), AGCD (BoM). Analysis: Climate Metrics Viewer v2.0. Always verify data and consult with climate scientists for decision-making.
